title: India A Bowl Nepal Out for 26 in 306-Run Rising Stars Win in Doha
excerpt: Centuries from Kumar Kushagra and Tilak Varma built 332 for 9 before Prince Yadav and Harshit Rana shared nine wickets in 11.3 overs, as Nepal posted the fifth-lowest total in List A history.
body:
• India A beat Nepal by 306 runs in Doha on Friday: 332 for 9 against 26 all out in 11.3 overs, in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars.
  • Kumar Kushagra (117 off 102) and captain Tilak Varma (107 off 113) added 206 for the fourth wicket after India A had slipped to 42 for 3.
  • Prince Yadav took 5 for 6 and Harshit Rana 4 for 16 with the new ball; no Nepal batter reached double figures.
  • Nepal's 26 is the fifth-lowest total in List A history. Because an A-team fixture carries List A status rather than ODI status, it does not enter the ODI record books.

Nepal were bowled out for 26 in 11.3 overs as India A opened their Asia Cup Rising Stars campaign with a 306-run win at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha on Friday. Chasing 333, Nepal lost both openers for ducks and were 4 wickets down with only 1 run on the board, undone by a new-ball spell in which Prince Yadav and Harshit Rana shared nine wickets.

Two centuries build the total

"The total will be quoted alongside the lowest scores in international cricket, but it does not belong in the ODI record list."

Nepal won the toss and fielded, and the decision looked sound when India A slipped to 42 for 3, with Abhishek Sharma and Ayush Badoni gone early and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi making 26. Captain Tilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra then rebuilt with a 206-run fourth-wicket partnership. Kushagra was bowled by Lalit Rajbanshi in the 43rd over for 117 off 102 balls, with 10 fours and five sixes, and Tilak fell in the 46th over for 107 off 113. Suryansh Shedge's unbeaten 36 off 14 balls pushed India A to 332 for 9, with 111 runs coming in the last 10 overs. Rajbanshi and Sandeep Lamichhane took 3 for 61 each for Nepal.

Eleven overs of collapse

Rana struck with the third ball of the chase, trapping Arjun Kumal lbw, and Nepal never recovered. Prince Yadav finished with 5 for 6 from five overs, Rana with 4 for 16 from six, and Shahbaz Ahmed took the final wicket, stumping Nandan Yadav off the third ball of the 12th over. Rashid Khan and Pawan Sarraf were Nepal's joint top scorers with 6 each. Nepal were also missing a few key players because of the ongoing Nepal Premier League, according to ESPNcricinfo's match report. Kushagra was named player of the match.

Why 26 is not an ODI record

The total will be quoted alongside the lowest scores in international cricket, but it does not belong in the ODI record list. Matches involving A teams carry List A status, not ODI status, and ESPNcricinfo records Nepal's 26 as the fifth-lowest total in List A history — and, as a senior national side, the second-lowest by a full national team in that format. For India A, the BCCI noted it was the side's largest victory by runs in List A cricket.

What it means and what's next

The win gives India A two points and a commanding net-run-rate start in Group B. Their campaign continues in Doha on Sunday against Pakistan Shaheens — our preview has the match details and how to watch. Nepal's hopes of reaching the semi-finals are dented but not ended in a group format, though they must regroup quickly after a defeat that will follow this young side for some time.
